cards.name: Color Management
cards.summary: Opens the Color Management dialog (bound to UnifiedColorManagementDialog), where CorelDRAW's color settings are set: default RGB, CMYK and grayscale profiles, rendering intent, color engine, and the policies for files opened or imported with a different or missing profile. Enabled with or without a document. Whether the same dialog also edits the active document's profiles is not shown in the harvest.
cards.how: Pick a preset or set the default RGB / CMYK / grayscale profiles, rendering intent and color engine; set the open and import policies (keep the embedded profile, convert to the document profile, or assign the default). Preserve pure black and map gray to CMYK black are the switches that matter for print.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("5a54114e-af98-4180-b7c5-a27e3532db1d"); without the dialog: Application.ColorManager properties (RenderingIntent, ColorEngine, PolicyForOpen, PolicyForImport, PreservePureBlack, MapGrayToCMYKBlack, DefaultColorContext) (unverified)
use_for: set the press CMYK profile before building a print brochure or packaging file
make imported RGB photos and logos convert predictably into a CMYK layout
match color settings with Photoshop / Illustrator in a mixed-app print workflow
avoid: re-profiling a half-finished document: colors shift; check with View/Proof Colors before committing
unattended runs: the dialog needs a person; set Application.ColorManager properties instead

cards.name: CorelDRAW
cards.summary: Opens the Options dialog at the CorelDRAW pages (Ctrl+J, bound to OnCorelDRAWOptions): preferences that belong to CorelDRAW itself, not to one document and not to the whole suite (that is Tools/Options/Global). Disabled only in full-screen preview. The page list is not in the harvest; from memory it covers general behavior, display, editing, text and save / auto-backup.
cards.how: Choose a page in the list on the left and change its settings; OK applies them to the application, so every file opened afterwards is affected. Settings stored with one file (page size, units, rulers, grid) are in Layout/Document Options instead.
use_for: turn on or shorten auto-backup before a long illustration job
set display and editing preferences once for every file instead of per document
tune text-editing behavior to a studio's habits
avoid: page size, units, rulers and grid of one file: those are document settings, use Layout/Document Options
automation: the dialog needs a person

review.changes: summary/how/use_for: dropped the unsourced claim that the Edit page holds nudge and duplicate offsets (from memory, in recent versions nudge sits with the per-document ruler settings, which this card's own avoid sends to Layout/Document Options); marked the page list as from memory, since the harvest only shows the OnCorelDRAWOptions binding

cards.name: Customization
cards.summary: Opens the Options dialog at the Customization pages (bound to OnCustomizationOptions), where the interface is tailored. Disabled in page sorter view and full-screen preview. The page list is from memory, not the harvest: commands (menu entries, toolbar buttons and their shortcut keys), command bars, the color palette display and the application's appearance.
cards.how: On the Commands page find a command, then assign or remove a shortcut key or change its caption and icon; on Command Bars show, create or reset toolbars. Changes are stored in the active workspace.
use_for: remap shortcuts to match habits from Illustrator or Photoshop
put a frequently used command or a saved script on a toolbar
build a lean toolbar for a repetitive production task
avoid: adopting another app's whole layout: switch to a ready-made workspace in Tools/Options/Workspaces instead of remapping by hand

review.changes: summary: marked the page list as from memory (the harvest only shows the OnCustomizationOptions binding)

cards.name: Global
cards.summary: Opens the Options dialog at the Global pages (bound to OnGraphicSuiteOptions): settings shared by the CorelDRAW Graphics Suite applications rather than CorelDRAW alone. From memory these include things like printing, file associations, import / export filters and bitmap-effect plug-ins; the exact page list is not in the harvest.
cards.how: Choose a page in the list on the left; a change here applies to the other suite apps that share it, not just CorelDRAW.
use_for: enable or trim the import / export file filters the suite offers
set which file types open in CorelDRAW from Windows
change suite-wide settings once instead of per app
avoid: CorelDRAW-only preferences: use Tools/Options/CorelDRAW (Ctrl+J)

cards.name: Tools
cards.summary: Opens the Options dialog at the Tools pages (bound to OnToolOptions), where the default behavior of the individual drawing and editing tools is set. Disabled only in full-screen preview. The per-tool pages are not in the harvest; from memory they include Pick tool behavior, Freehand / Bezier smoothing and auto-join, polygon and star points, and eraser, knife, dimension and connector settings.
cards.how: Pick a tool in the list and change its defaults; they apply to the next use of that tool. Double-clicking some toolbox tools also opens their page here, but not all: a double-click on the Pick tool selects all objects instead.
use_for: set curve smoothing and auto-join distance before tracing a sketch
set default polygon / star points for a badge or seal
make the Pick tool behave the way a studio expects
avoid: changing one object: use the tool's property bar instead of the defaults

review.changes: summary: marked the per-tool page list as from memory; how: 'double-clicking many tools opens the same page' overclaimed (Pick tool double-click selects all), now says some tools, with the exception named

cards.name: Workspaces
cards.summary: Opens the Options dialog at the Workspaces page, which lists the installed workspaces (for example Default, Illustration and an Adobe Illustrator-style layout) and lets you switch, create, delete, import or export them. Disabled only in full-screen preview.
cards.how: Tick a workspace to make it active; New / Delete / Import / Export manage the list (.cdws files). The same jobs sit under Window/Workspace.
use_for: switch to an Illustrator-like layout for a designer coming from Adobe
export a studio workspace so every seat has the same menus and shortcuts
go back to the default layout after heavy customization
avoid: a quick switch: Window/Workspace is faster than the Options dialog

cards.name: Save Settings as Default
cards.summary: Saves the current settings as the defaults that new documents and later sessions start from. Needs an open document and is disabled in page sorter view and full-screen preview. Which settings are included (styles, default object properties, page and document settings) is from memory, and the harvest flags a dialog without showing what it asks, presumably a confirmation or a choice of what to save.
cards.how: Set up a document the way new work should start, then run the command and confirm the dialog.
use_for: make a house page size, units and styles the starting point of every new file
keep default fill and outline after setting up a studio standard
avoid: settings for one kind of project only: use File/Save as Template instead
a shared machine: it changes the defaults for everyone who uses this profile

review.changes: summary: added the batch's other enable conditions (off in page sorter view and full-screen preview)

cards.name: Cancel Recording
cards.summary: Stops the script recording in progress and throws it away, so nothing is saved. Only enabled while a recording runs, so it was disabled in every probed state here.
use_for: abandon a recording after a wrong step instead of saving a broken script
avoid: keeping what was recorded: use Stop Recording (Ctrl+Shift+O)

cards.name: Pause Recording
cards.summary: Check item that suspends the script recording in progress, so steps taken while paused are not recorded; clearing it resumes recording. Only enabled while recording, so disabled in every probed state here.
use_for: change the view or set up a selection mid-recording without capturing those steps
avoid: forgetting to resume: steps done while paused are missing from the script

cards.name: Record Temporary Script
cards.summary: Starts recording a temporary script at once, without asking for a name or a project. It is replayed with Run Temporary Script (Ctrl+Shift+P), ended with Stop Recording (Ctrl+Shift+O), and replaced by the next temporary recording.
use_for: repeat a fiddly multi-step edit across many objects in one session
try out a sequence before saving it as a named script
avoid: anything to keep or share: use Start Recording to save a named script

cards.name: Run Script
cards.summary: Opens the Run Script dialog, which lists the scripts (macros) in the loaded script projects (GMS files); select one and run it. Enabled with or without a document.
cards.how: Choose the project to list scripts from, select the script, then Run.
use_for: run a saved production script such as batch export or renaming
run a script that has no toolbar button or shortcut
avoid: unattended pipelines: call GMSManager.RunMacro instead of the dialog

cards.name: Run Temporary Script
cards.summary: Plays back the last script recorded with Record Temporary Script, repeating the same steps on the current document or selection. Enabled in every probed state (no document, document, rectangle, bitmap); the harvest does not show whether a temporary script existed at probe time, so enabled is no proof there is something to play.
use_for: apply the same multi-step edit to object after object with one shortcut
avoid: before recording one: there is nothing to play
steps that depend on a specific selection: the replay acts on whatever is selected now

review.changes: summary: removed the claim that it was enabled 'even when no temporary script has been recorded yet'; the batch only records the four enabled states, not whether a temporary recording existed

cards.name: Script Editor
cards.summary: Opens the Microsoft Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) editor attached to CorelDRAW, where script projects and recorded scripts are read, edited, debugged and written. Enabled in every probed state, so VBA is installed on the harvest machine.
cards.how: The project tree lists the loaded GMS projects; recorded scripts appear as VBA modules. Run or step through code from the editor.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("28e16db6-6339-440d-af0d-f58ac27c115d"); code access without the editor: Application.VBE (unverified)
use_for: clean up a recorded script into a reusable production macro
write or debug VBA automation for CorelDRAW
avoid: installs without the VBA component: the command is unavailable
.NET add-ons: use Visual Studio Editor

cards.name: Scripts
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Scripts docker, which lists the loaded script projects and their scripts so you can run, edit, record, load or unload them. Same toggle as Window/Dockers/Scripts.
use_for: keep production scripts one double-click away during a job
load a colleague's GMS project and run its scripts
avoid: running one known script from automation: use GMSManager.RunMacro, the docker is UI only

cards.name: Start Recording
cards.summary: Starts recording your actions as a named script stored in a script project, to be replayed later from Run Script or the Scripts docker. CorelDRAW normally asks first for the script name and the project to save it in; the harvest does not flag a dialog for this item, so that prompt is from memory.
cards.how: Give the script a name, pick the project to store it in, then work; end with Stop Recording (Ctrl+Shift+O), or throw it away with Cancel Recording.
use_for: capture a repeated production sequence (resize, recolor, export) as a reusable script
make a starting point for a VBA macro, then refine it in the Script Editor
avoid: a one-off repeat in this session: Record Temporary Script (Ctrl+Shift+R) skips the naming step
steps that do not record (some dialogs and dockers): check the result in the Script Editor

cards.name: Stop Recording
cards.summary: Ends the recording in progress and keeps it: a named script is saved to its project, a temporary one becomes what Run Temporary Script plays. Only enabled while recording, so disabled in every probed state here.
use_for: finish and keep a recorded production sequence
avoid: a recording that went wrong: use Cancel Recording so the bad steps are not saved

cards.name: Visual Studio Editor
cards.summary: Opens Microsoft Visual Studio through CorelDRAW's VSTA integration to write .NET (C# / VB.NET) scripts and add-ons. Enabled in every probed state here; it relies on a compatible Visual Studio being installed.
cards.how: Create or open a VSTA project; the CorelDRAW object model is referenced so the code drives the open document.
use_for: build a .NET add-on or docker for a CorelDRAW production pipeline
port VBA automation to C#
avoid: quick edits to a recorded script: Script Editor (Alt+F11) opens VBA directly
machines without Visual Studio: nothing useful opens
